item.title: Eisenkot tipped to seek Israel government as religious party drops Netanyahu
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot emerged on Thursday as the favourite to be tasked with trying to form an Israeli government as a religious party long aligned with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declined to recommend him. President Isaac Herzog was holding a second day of consultations with political parties after the October 27 election, in which neither Netanyahu — a polarising right-winger who has led Israel through three years of war — nor Eisenkot — a former military chief promising to restore national unity — secured enough votes for a majority. Herzog will choose by himself whom to ask to form a new government but traditionally the mandate is given to the person recommended by more parties, which would be Eisenkot. The opposition leader also received a recommendation from a key lawmaker from the Israeli-Arab minority, whose seats in parliament soared due to outrage over Netanyahu’s policies, even as Eisenkot has remained unclear on whether he would accept Arab support to form a government. United Torah Judaism, which backed Netanyahu after the previous five elections, in its meeting with Herzog declined to recommend Netanyahu again as prime minister, although it also did not side with Eisenkot. The party informed Herzog “that it has decided not to recommend any member of Knesset to form a government,” the president’s office said in a statement, referring to the 120-member parliament in which United Torah Judaism has won seven seats. The party — which represents ultra-Orthodox Jews of Ashkenazi origin, who mostly hail from or have roots in Europe — as well as Shas — which represents the same community but of Sephardic, or mostly Middle Eastern and North African descent — have both been backed by Netanyahu as they push to maintain the exemption from military service for religious students. Netanyahu has preserved the exemption but stopped short of enshrining it in law, in the face of major resentment from many other Israelis as reservists serve multiple tours due to the wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. “In whatever government is next formed, our immediate item is sorting out the status of Torah students,” United Torah Judaism lawmaker Isaac Pindrus said. Eisenkot, who has tried to appeal to secular Israelis from left to right, has been adamant about closing exemptions to military service. Some of his opposition allies have criticised the ultra-Orthodox, who make up about 14 percent of the population but have far higher birthrates than secular Israelis, as a drain on the state. Observers say United Torah Judaism’s tactic is likely aimed mostly at punishing Netanyahu and showing that their votes cannot be taken for granted, while they would still serve in a government if he were to form one. – Arab-Israelis play key role – Once Herzog gives his mandate to a lawmaker, the person — presumably either Eisenkot or Netanyahu — will have 28 days to form a government, with a potential 14-day extension. If the lawmaker fails, Herzog will then task someone else. Netanya

item.title: Edo Moves To Launch State-Owned Airline As Okpebholo Signs MoU
item.description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, moved a step closer to establishing a state-owned airline on Wednesday by signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with China Express Airline Co. Ltd and KDN Aero. The governor signed the agreement at Government House, Benin City, with representatives of the Chinese airline led by its President, Shansheng Li, following a presentation on the company’s operational capacity. He said the carrier would be operating “very soon.” Expressing satisfaction with the proposed partnership and describing the MoU as the beginning of a longer relationship, Okpebholo said, “We have signed the MoU, and this is the first part of it. We will continue to build on it. “A presentation was made, which was very beautiful and wonderful. We have seen your capability, and we are ready to do business with you. By the grace of God, Edo Air will be in the airspace very soon. So, we are in partnership with you.” He stated Secretary to the State Government (SSG), Umar Musa Ikhilor, Esq., said the agreement followed a fact-finding trip to China by a seven-man delegation on September 14, 2026, approved by the governor to meet potential technical and operational partners for the proposed airline. Ikhilor led the delegation, which included the Head of Service, Dr Anthony Okungbowa; the Accountant-General, Julius Anelu; and the Chief Aviation Consultant to the Edo State Government, Captain Nuhu Musa. Other government officials and aviation experts were also on the team. He said the delegation visited China Express Airline and the Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China (COMAC), the country’s major aircraft manufacturer, to assess their capabilities and explore areas of cooperation. Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, moved a step closer to establishing a state-owned airline on Wednesday by signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with China Express Airline Co. Ltd and KDN Aero. Of the two organisations, Ikhilor said China Express left a stronger impression on the delegation. At the airline’s headquarters, the team toured its flight-monitoring operations. He said the situation room had a giant screen tracking flights across China, with 192 flights already logged by 10 a.m. on the day of the visit. The SSG said the facilities inspected and discussions with the airline’s management convinced the delegation that China Express was a suitable technical and operational partner for Edo Air. He expressed hope that the MoU and further engagements would lay the foundation for concrete steps towards realising the governor’s plan to establish an Edo-owned airline. At the Government House event, Li presented the governor with a model aircraft, while the Managing Director of KDY AERO, Tianzhi Chen, spoke on behalf of the Chinese delegation and took the audience through the airline’s operations and capabilities. item.title: Leave EFCC out of politics, Kogi group warns Obi-Kwankwaso Movement
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — The Kogi Central Progressive Elites have warned the Obi-Kwankwaso Movement against dragging the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) into partisan politics following its call for an investigation into Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan’s recent cash empowerment programme. The group described the call as a politically motivated attempt to undermine the lawmaker ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement issued in Abuja on Thursday, its President, Abdullahi Omeiza, said the group was concerned about what it described as the growing tendency among political actors to deploy anti-corruption institutions and rhetoric for partisan purposes. He said: “We are concerned about the growing tendency among some political actors to deploy anti-corruption institutions and rhetoric as instruments of partisan warfare. “Accountability is important, but it must be pursued through facts, evidence and established legal procedures, not through sensational political narratives designed to damage the reputation of an elected public official.” The group argued that constituency empowerment programmes should not automatically be classified as vote-buying simply because they involve direct financial assistance to beneficiaries. It said such initiatives could be subjected to legitimate scrutiny, but insisted that any investigation must be guided by evidence and the law. “The mere distribution of financial assistance to constituents does not, in itself, establish an offence of vote-buying,” the statement added. On the demand for an EFCC investigation and prosecution, the group acknowledged that no one was above the law but cautioned against turning anti-corruption agencies into instruments of political intimidation. Omeiza said: “Accountability is indispensable to democratic governance, but it must never become a convenient weapon for settling political scores. “Allegations are not convictions, petitions are not proof of wrongdoing, and public accusations cannot substitute for due process. “The EFCC must be allowed to discharge its statutory responsibilities independently, without being subjected to political pressure or media-driven prejudgement.” The group challenged the Obi-Kwankwaso Movement to submit any credible evidence to the appropriate authorities rather than rely on public declarations and what it described as inflammatory narratives. It also maintained that the people of Kogi Central had the right to assess Akpoti-Uduaghan’s performance and determine whether she deserved another term. “The people of Kogi Central are politically conscious, discerning and capable of evaluating their representative. They understand the difference between constructive criticism and politically motivated attacks. “No pressure group, political organisation or individual can arrogate to itself the authority to determine the political destiny of our senatorial district,” Omeiza said. item.title: Kidnappers demand N25m for nine corps members, driver abducted in Ogun
item.description: By Adeola Badru Families of 10 travellers, including nine members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) and a driver, have appealed to the Federal Government and security agencies to secure their release after they were abducted along the Ijebu-Ode–Ibadan road in Ogun State. The kidnappers have demanded a ransom of N25 million and reportedly given the families a Thursday deadline to pay. One of the victims, identified as Dapo, is a recently discharged corps member who completed his national service in Edo State last week. He was reportedly travelling to Ibadan when the incident occurred on Tuesday. His sister, Abigeal, who raised the alarm, said the family had been thrown into distress following the abduction, particularly as they lacked the means to raise the demanded ransom. According to her, the victims were travelling from Ijebu-Ode towards Ibadan when their vehicle was attacked shortly after 7pm. She said her brother had been updating the family about his journey until he sent a video showing the traffic situation on the road, which turned out to be their last communication with him. Abigeal said the family learnt of the abduction after one of the corps members travelling in the vehicle escaped and contacted another family member shortly after 7pm on Tuesday. She said: “On Tuesday, my brother was on his way back from Edo. He was posted to Edo State for NYSC and did his passing-out ceremony last week. So, he was on his way back to Ibadan. “He was still giving us updates about his journey. At some point, he posted that there was traffic. I have the videos on my phone. That was the last time we heard from him. “Not until around past 7pm, when one of the corps members escaped. I don’t know how he escaped. “I also spoke to that guy yesterday. He was the one who told another brother of mine that their bus was attacked and they had been kidnapped, my brother and nine other people.” She said the family was informed that police officers and local vigilantes had launched a search operation in the forest shortly after the incident but expressed concern that the operation had yet to yield any breakthrough. According to her, the family visited the Ijebu-Ode Police Station on Wednesday to report the incident and seek information about the victims. She said the police initially asked them to remain calm, explaining that their personnel were still searching the forest. However, the operatives reportedly returned less than an hour later without any information about the abducted travellers. Abigeal said the family was subsequently advised to await contact from the kidnappers. She said that while they were returning from the police station to the motor park, the abductors called using her brother’s mobile phone. The family reportedly returned to the police station, where they heard Dapo’s voice before the kidnappers took over the conversation and demanded N20 million. item.title: UK to hold talks on harms of slave trade
item.description: Commonwealth leaders have welcomed Britain’s agreement to engage in “time-bound inclusive and good-faith dialogue” over the “historical harms” of the transatlantic slave trade. In a final communique issued late on Wednesday, the group of nations said the time had come for “meaningful, truthful and respectful conversation towards forging a common future based on equity”. But it did not set out a timetable for the talks. It comes after British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was open to saying sorry but ruled out paying financial reparations demanded by some Caribbean countries. Burnham used his appearance at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda to hold discussions about issuing a formal apology for Britain’s role in slavery, which saw about 10-15 million slaves brought from Africa to the Americas over four centuries. In a speech to opening the biannual Commonwealth leaders meeting on Tuesday, King Charles III, who is politically neutral, called the slave trade “a monstrous injustice” that filled him with “profound personal sorrow”, stopping short of a formal apology. Britain’s pivotal part in slavery has long strained relations between the UK and its former colonies, including an awkward previous meeting of Commonwealth leaders in 2024. “We welcome the agreement of the government of the United Kingdom to engage in a structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith dialogue with affected parties addressing the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans and its historical harms,” the final communique said. The Commonwealth is a 56-nation group of mostly former British colonies. Of those Charles remains head of state in 14. Britain’s Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has said it is “not feasible” for the country to pay reparations for slavery, but that “there are things we can work on co-operatively”. Miliband also hinted that Britain could issue a formal apology next year when it hosts a G20 leaders’ summit, in comments to the BBC aired on Wednesday as the meeting wrapped up. item.title: KEDI Healthcare Celebrates 20 Years in Nigeria with 8th Car Award Ceremony and Major Announcements
item.description: KEDI Healthcare Industries Nigeria Limited celebrated its 20th anniversary alongside its 8th Car Award Ceremony on 24 October 2026 at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts (formerly the National Theatre), Iganmu, Lagos. Held under the theme “A Grand Celebration of Excellence & Global Impact” and the slogan “BIGGER. BETTER. GREATER.”, the event brought together distributors, business partners, distinguished guests and stakeholders from Nigeria and other African countries to celebrate two decades of growth, entrepreneurship and community impact. Recognizing Excellence and Distributor Achievements The highlight of the celebration was KEDI’s 8th Car Award Ceremony, recognizing outstanding distributors for their business achievements and contributions to the company’s growth. The ceremony celebrated Car Awardees from Nigeria and Ghana, alongside distributors recognized across various categories, including outstanding consultants, managers, directors, service centres, lecturers and business teams. Special recognition was given to KEDI’s three Honorary Chairmen — Chief Chinedu Sunny Ojiaku, Mr. Adegbemisoye Zion and Mr. Ajala Eniola — for their exceptional contributions to the company’s development. Through its recognition programmes, business training and distributor support initiatives, KEDI continues to encourage entrepreneurship, leadership development and long-term business growth. Celebrating 20 Years and Unveiling a Renewed Corporate Direction Established in 2006, KEDI Healthcare has developed a strong presence in Nigeria and expanded its business network into other African markets, including Ghana, Benin Republic and Liberia. During the anniversary celebration, KEDI’s Operations Director, Mr. Roger Luo, acknowledged the contributions of distributors, employees and business partners throughout the company’s 20-year journey. He also introduced KEDI’s renewed corporate mission and vision, reflecting the company’s ambition to combine traditional medicine wisdom with modern health and beauty solutions while empowering business partners through opportunities for growth and shared prosperity. The company’s new vision is “To become the world’s most trusted health and wellness platform, empowering lives with total well-being, success, and vitality.” The event also introduced Road to Africa , a book written by KEDI’s Founder and Chairman, Mr. William Zhao, documenting his experiences and entrepreneurial journey in Africa. The Chinese edition has been published, with an English edition expected to follow. Aloe House: Expanding into Beauty and Wellness Another major announcement was the unveiling of Aloe House, a new beauty and wellness project developed through a partnership between KEDI Healthcare and AGHG in the United States. Inspired by aloe, the project represents KEDI’s strategic expansion into skincare, haircare, personal care and other beauty-related products and services. item.title: Kane becomes highest-paid footballer in Europe after new deal
item.description: England captain Harry Kane has signed a record-breaking contract extension with Bayern Munich that will keep him at the German club until June 2029, in a deal reportedly making him the highest-paid player in Europe by basic salary. According to David Ornstein of The Athletic , the three-year extension is the most lucrative contract in Bayern Munich’s history, although some European players could still earn more than the striker when performance-related bonuses are included. The 33-year-old’s previous contract was due to expire next summer, but both Kane and the Bundesliga champions were keen to continue their partnership. Bayern reportedly do not consider the new agreement his final contract, with the club keen to retain the England international for the foreseeable future. Speaking after signing the extension, Kane expressed his satisfaction with life in Munich, describing his relationship with the club, supporters and city as a special one. “I feel right at home at FC Bayern. I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich,” he said. “We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager. It makes me very proud to be part of this club. My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. “I’m now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club.” The contract extension comes after a remarkable period for the striker, who won the Ballon d’Or in late October, becoming the first English player to receive the prestigious award since 2001. He is also expected to become England’s most-capped player during the November international break. Since joining Bayern from Tottenham Hotspur three years ago, Kane has scored 156 goals in 161 appearances, establishing himself as one of the club’s most influential players. During his time in Germany, he has won two Bundesliga titles, the DFB-Pokal and two Supercups. However, winning the UEFA Champions League remains a major ambition for the England captain as he looks to add Europe’s biggest club competition to his collection of honours. His decision to extend his stay in Germany also appears to have dealt a significant blow to hopes of him returning to the Premier League to challenge Alan Shearer’s all-time scoring record. With his Bayern future secured until 2029, Kane looks increasingly likely to prioritise further success in Germany over a return to English football. item.title: 5 takeaways from Ronaldo’s retirement speech to Portugal
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo has announced the end of his 23-year journey with the Portugal national team, reflecting on his achievements, sacrifices and enduring connection with the country. In an emotional farewell message addressed to the Portuguese people, the five-time Ballon d’Or winner described representing his country as the greatest honour of his career, while expressing gratitude to his teammates, coaches, family and supporters. Here are five key takeaways from Ronaldo’s retirement speech. 1. Ronaldo brings his 23-year Portugal career to an end Ronaldo confirmed that his journey with the Portugal national team, which began in August 2003, had come to an end. The 41-year-old said it was time to hand over the national team shirt and captain’s armband to the next generation after 23 years of representing his country. He described the decision as difficult, saying it was one guided not only by his head but also by his heart. 2. He considers representing Portugal his greatest achievement Despite spending much of his career pursuing individual records and becoming the best player in the world, Ronaldo said his greatest victory was earning the honour of representing Portugal. Reflecting on his journey, he said: “I spent my life working to become the best player in the world. Today, I realize that my greatest victory was earning the honor of representing the best country in the world.” 3. He acknowledged his failures and sacrifices Ronaldo admitted that his international career was not without disappointments, recalling defeats, difficult moments and occasions when he could not deliver the results Portuguese supporters wanted. However, he maintained that he never gave up or stopped feeling proud of representing his country. He also acknowledged the sacrifices made by his family, teammates and the support staff who contributed to his 23-year journey. 4. He urged Portugal’s next generation to keep dreaming The former Portugal captain called on young players to continue believing in their abilities and push the country’s footballing ambitions further. He stressed the importance of producing new heroes and inspiring future generations to achieve what previous generations could not. “Portugal will always need young people who dream, players who never give up, and new generations who believe it is possible to reach places no one has reached before,” he said. 5. He promised to continue supporting Portugal after retirement Although his playing career with the national team has ended, Ronaldo said his emotional connection with Portugal would remain unchanged. He recalled the powerful feeling of standing alongside teammates and supporters during the national anthem, describing it as a moment when differences in social class, profession, opinions and football allegiance disappear. item.title: Wike distances self from court ruling favouring Okorocha over Uzodimma
item.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has dismissed claims that he influenced the court judgment which recognised former Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha as the All Progressives Congress candidate for Imo West Senatorial District in the 2027 elections. Wike spoke during a live media chat on Thursday in Port Harcourt, where he described the allegations as mischievous, stressing that he neither filed the suit nor had any involvement in the legal proceedings. “First of all, anybody calling my name is being mischievous. I didn’t go to court. I’m not in APC. I don’t know what the issue is,” he said. Wike also reacted to reports that Governor Hope Uzodimma had warned, a day before the judgment, that he would seize the vehicles of anyone promoting the proposed Rainbow Coalition in Imo State. Describing the reported warning as uncivilised, the minister said: “They were saying that because a day before that judgment was given, he had openly warned people that, ‘No Rainbow Coalition here. If I see… I’ll collect the vehicle for you.’ Very, very uncivilised.” He also clarified a video circulating online showing him dancing with Okorocha, saying it was recorded when he hosted the former governor while he was still in office. “Now they showed the video where Rochas and I danced when I hosted him when he was governor. So that was that dance,” Wike said. The controversy followed a Federal High Court judgment in Abuja directing the Independent National Electoral Commission to recognise Okorocha as the APC candidate for Imo West Senatorial District in the 2027 general election. Justice Obiora Egwuatu ruled that Okorocha emerged winner of the party’s senatorial primary held on May 18, 2026, rather than Uzodimma, and ordered INEC to substitute the governor’s name with that of the former governor. The case was instituted by Okorocha, who challenged INEC’s recognition of Uzodimma as the winner of the primary. The court held that the evidence presented showed that Okorocha secured the majority of valid votes cast. The ruling has been contested by the Imo State chapter of the APC, while Uzodimma has indicated plans to appeal. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from international football
item.description: Portuguese football legend Cristiano Ronaldo announced on Thursday that he was retiring from international football at the age of 41. Ronaldo played 234 times for Portugal and scored 146 goals — a world record. But the forward’s powers have been waning in recent years and he fell out with national coach Jorge Jesus last month after he refused to play him in a Nations League match. Ronaldo immediately left the team camp and was handed a 30-day suspension. Although it was rumoured that he intended to return to the international fold, on Thursday the five-time winner of the Ballon d’Or released a video on his Instagram account in which he said he was ending his international career. “To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team,” Ronaldo said, as images of his career were played. “I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world,” he continued. “Today the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the mind alone — they are also made with the heart. “A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end,” he added. In the highlight of his international career, Ronaldo won the European Championship with Portugal in 2016 in France, although he had to leave the field during the final with an injury. At this year’s World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico, he scored three goals but Portugal were knocked out in the Round of 16 by eventual winners Spain. item.title: Zelensky says hopes US election means more support for Ukraine
item.description: Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky has said he hoped the Democrat triumph in the US midterm elections would boost support for Kyiv and help end the war with Russia. Ukraine and its European allies had been worried about the United States getting closer to Russia since President Donald Trump returned to the White House last year. Ties between Trump and Zelensky have been turbulent, with tensions rising in recent weeks as the US leader criticised Kyiv and made a deal with President Vladimir Putin to ease sanctions in return for the release of Russian diesel. “There is hope now that there is this balance of power, and that we will be supported more,” Zelensky told German broadcaster ZDF in an interview broadcast late Wednesday. Zelensky said that if the US Congress “starts talking about strong financial support or military support” it would “influence Putin.” “And Putin will be thinking about whether it makes sense to keep fighting if the support will only grow. Logically, this will (lead) us to possible negotiations and a possible peace,” he said. US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks are to be held next week in Abu Dhabi. The talks had been frozen since the Middle East war erupted in February. Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner have been leading the negotiations amid criticism over their attitude to Russia. item.title: Court sacks Mark-led ADC exco, voids Atiku’s candidacy
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja The Federal High Court in Abuja has sacked the Senator David Mark-led executives of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and invalidated all actions they took on behalf of the party. The actions included the nomination of a former vice president, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, as the party’s presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections. Atiku, whose name was earlier published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) as a candidate for the presidential poll, has since chosen a former governor of Rivers State, Rotimi Amaechi, as his running mate. However, in a judgment delivered on Thursday by Justice Peter Lifu, the court declared illegal the Senator Mark-led Caretaker Committee of the ADC, which organised the primary election that produced Atiku as the party’s presidential flag bearer. The court found merit in a suit brought before it by the aggrieved former National Deputy Chairman (North-East) of the party, Nafiu Bala Gombe. Gombe had approached the court to query the process through which the Senator Mark-led Committee took over the reins of leadership of the party. He maintained that, with the resignation of the former National Chairman, Chief Ralph Nwosu, he (Gombe) was qualified to assume the party’s leadership. Consequently, he, among other things, prayed the court to nullify all actions taken on behalf of the party by the Senator Mark-led leadership. Listed as defendants in the suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, were the ADC, INEC, Senator Mark, Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola and Chief Ralph Nwosu. The plaintiff further urged the court to restrain Senator Mark and Aregbesola from parading themselves as National Chairman and Secretary, respectively, of the ADC, insisting that their emergence violated the party’s constitution and the provisions of the Electoral Act. The court upheld the plaintiff’s claim and granted his reliefs, a verdict that could spark a chain of reactions in the polity, with the presidential election scheduled for January 16, 2027. Already, the ADC has vowed to appeal the judgment. Reacting to the outcome of the case, the National Welfare Secretary of the ADC, Mr. Nkemakolam Ukandu, who was later joined as an interested party in the matter, said the verdict would be challenged at the appellate court. The development comes barely 24 hours after the party’s candidate, Atiku, held a massive rally in Sokoto State as part of his campaign for the 2027 presidential election. item.title: Netanyahu loses religious party’s support as rival tipped to form government
item.description: An ultra-Orthodox Jewish party long aligned with Benjamin Netanyahu declined on Thursday to recommend him to stay as Israel’s prime minister, as signs grew that rival Gadi Eisenkot will have the first chance to form a government. President Isaac Herzog was holding a second day of consultations with political parties after the October 27 election, in which neither Netanyahu — a polarising right-winger who has led Israel through three years of war — nor Eisenkot secured enough votes for a majority. United Torah Judaism, which backed Netanyahu after the previous five elections, in its meeting with Herzog declined to recommend Netanyahu again as prime minister, although it also did not side with Eisenkot. The party informed Herzog “that it has decided not to recommend any member of Knesset to form a government,” the president’s office said in a statement, referring to the 120-member parliament in which United Torah Judaism has won seven seats. The party, which represents ultra-Orthodox Jews of Ashkenazi origin, who mostly hail from or have roots in Europe, as well as Shas, which represents the same community but of Sephardic, or mostly Middle Eastern and North African descent, have both been backed by Netanyahu as they push to maintain the exemption from military service for religious students. Netanyahu has preserved the exemption but stopped short of enshrining it in law, in the face of major resentment from many other Israelis as reservists serve multiple tours due to the wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. “In whatever government is next formed, our immediate item is sorting out the status of Torah students,” United Torah Judaism lawmaker Isaac Pindrus said. Eisenkot, a former military chief seeking to unite the centre and centre-right, has been adamant about closing exemptions to military service, with some of his opposition allies harshly criticising the ultra-Orthodox as self-serving. Observers say United Torah Judaism’s approach may be aimed more at punishing Netanyahu and showing that their votes cannot be taken for granted, while they could still serve in a government if he were to form one. Herzog will meet representatives of the major parties later on Thursday before tasking one lawmaker with forming a government. He generally bases his decision on which person receives the most party recommendations, making it likely he will ask Eisenkot. Once Herzog gives the mandate, that lawmaker will have 28 days to form a government, with a potential 14-day extension. If the lawmaker fails, Herzog will then task someone else. Netanyahu’s bloc — including United Torah Judaism — has 53 seats in the new parliament, as opposed to 48 for Eisenkot’s bloc. Israeli-Arab parties soared in strength on the back of anger over Netanyahu’s hard-right government, winning 19 seats. item.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has stated his position on the recent Federal High Court Judgement which nullified the recognition of the current governor of Imo State, Hope Uzodimma, as the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Imo-West senatorial district in the 2027 general elections. Speaking during his ongoing media chat in Portharcourt, Rivers State, on Thursday, Wike dismissed his involvement in the court judgement, stating that those linking his name are only being mischievous Though he admitted publicly disagreeing with the Governor of Imo, Hope Uzodinma, over his rainbow coalition initiative, he denied being in the know of ongoing internal political issues in the APC. Further speaking on his rainbow coalition initiative, Wike posed a question to the Imo State Governor, asking, “What is Uzodimma afraid of?” “I didn’t go to court; I’m not from APC. People are saying that because a day before that judgement he had openly warned his people there’s no Rainbow Coalition; if I see you I’ll collect the vehicle. So when the judgement came, they said it was me. How could it have been me? What is Hope Uzodinma afraid of in the Rainbow Coalition?” He said both priorities should be working to see the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in 2027, adding that if there is an initiative to achieve that, “What then is the issue?” he asked. “Your business is to make sure Mr President wins elections. At the national assembly level, so many factors come in, including zoning. I owe no apologies that Rochas is my friend; after all, he has friends in Rivers State that are my political enemies; will I go and kill them? No!!” “If he’s a strong man, he shouldn’t be afraid. item.title: Race for 2028 heats up after US midterms firestorm
item.description: President Donald Trump’s stunning midterms defeat by the Democrats has upended another US election — the race to replace him in the White House in 2028. The crushing defeat for the Republicans is particularly stinging for Vice President JD Vance, who had been the frontrunner but now risks being seen as tied to his lame-duck boss. But the midterms are a potential launchpad for rising Democratic stars like Georgia senator Jon Ossoff, whose youthful vibe has already drawn comparisons to former president Barack Obama. – Republicans in turmoil – The MAGA coalition that shot Trump to power in 2016 and 2024 effectively collapsed in Tuesday’s midterms, leaving any presumptive Republican heir with a mountain to climb. Long seen as the odds-on favorite for the Republican nomination in 2028, Vance is the most obvious victim after hitching his wagon to Trump throughout the midterms campaigns with rallies in swing states. The ambitious 42-year-old quickly tried to distance himself from the electoral disaster, blaming it on Trump’s unpopular war on Iran in a long thesis posted on X on Wednesday. But voters are likely to reject his attempts to disown Trump. It’s a familiar problem for US vice presidents. Former Democratic candidate and vice president Kamala Harris suffered from a similar problem in 2024 when she said that “there’s not a thing that comes to mind” when asked how she’d differentiate herself from Joe Biden. “The bad news for Vance is that sitting vice presidents seldom win the presidency,” James Lindsay of the Council for Foreign Relations, said. Trump’s Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s name has also been bandied about. Rubio, 55, has kept a far lower profile during the midterms but any top official in Trump’s administration will struggle to wash their hands of the Iran war. The Republicans’ midterm disaster could, however, be a boost for other possible candidates. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, 48, who ran against Trump for the Republican nomination in 2024, has suddenly become very vocal. He described the Democratic sweep as “the political equivalent of a meteor strike” — and pointed out that it was only in his own state that Republicans held them off. Texas Senator Ted Cruz, 55, has also left the door open, having run against Trump in 2016 — although his chances may have been harmed by the Democrats’ stunning senate and governor wins in the midterms in his state. – Democrats on a high – The Democratic field is crowded but the midterms have given some likely candidates a boost. Ossoff’s reelection as Georgia Senator has fueled speculation about a 2028 run by a telegenic politician who has already gained attention for mocking Trump’s relationship with a young staffer. The 39-year-old has said that he has “zero interest in running for president” but his swiftly-declared win in Georgia — and his victory speech — have bolstered his status in the party. item.title: ‘I’m PDP member but Wike is not my leader’ — Oyinlola
item.description: Former Osun State Governor, Olagunsoye Oyinlola, has dissociated himself from the Peoples Democratic Party leadership purportedly under the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, saying the minister is not his leader. Oyinlola, a retired general, stated this on Wednesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today programme. When asked whether Wike was his leader in the PDP, the former governor said, “No, not my leader. You don’t say that kind of thing.” He added, “Yes, I am a member of the PDP, but he’s not my leader.” Oyinlola also suggested that Wike was young enough to be his political subordinate, citing their different stages of life when he served as military governor of Lagos State between 1993 and 1996. Asked whether Wike was his boy, he said, “He qualifies to be. When I was governor in Lagos, where was he? In school.” Wike, a PDP member, was appointed FCT minister by President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC). He subsequently established the Rainbow coalition, a political structure backing Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027. The coalition has attracted criticism from some PDP members who accuse Wike of working against the party’s interests by supporting the president. Oyinlola, who governed Osun from 2003 to 2010, also blamed the crisis rocking the opposition party on internal forces working against efforts to restore its unity. Speaking about former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s efforts to rebuild the party, Oyinlola said the former president had been working to re-engineer its structure, but some members were frustrating the process. “He’s been trying to ensure that the party is re-engineered. But those who don’t want it are working against it within the party. That’s the much I can say,” he said. Oyinlola maintained that the PDP remained capable of recovering from its internal crisis, noting that it had structures across the country. “The PDP is not dead. The bone will rise again,” he said. He added that the party had a presence in all 774 local government areas and could regain its strength if members resolved their differences. “If we get our acts together, it’s a thing we can achieve, but the forces making sure we don’t get there are there. They are not sleeping,” Oyinlola said. The post ‘I’m PDP member but Wike is not my leader’ — Oyinlola appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Canada unveils budget to curb reliance on US
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government presents its budget on Thursday, a plan designed to reduce US reliance, which remains Ottawa’s priority despite President Donald Trump’s midterm election setback. Carney has argued that relations between Canada and the United States have been permanently altered and that pre-Trump tariff-free relations will not return. Carney says Canada needs to urgently diversify its trade relationships and has named Thursday’s budget — his second since taking office last year — “Masters of our Destiny.” “At its core, our plan is about changing Canada’s growth model,” Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne said this week. Champagne, who will present the budget to parliament, added that the goals include boosting domestic commerce within Canada and “diversifying our trade.” “No matter what happens south of the border, no matter what happens in the world, we will be more resilient, we will be stronger, we will be more independent,” Champagne said Wednesday, after selecting a new pair of shoes for his budget speech, keeping a quirky Canadian tradition. Trump’s tariffs have battered Canada’s economy but the future of his protectionist trade measures faced fresh uncertainty after his Republican Party suffered a crushing midterm defeat. Democrats, who have been critical of tariffs on Canada, will take control of both the US House and Senate next year. Senior Democratic Congressman Jamie Raskin told Canada’s public broadcaster CBC on Wednesday that his party is “going to put an end to these tariffs” and will be seeking to repair ties “with our best friends like Canada.” But Canada’s minister responsible for US trade, Dominic LeBlanc, noted Wednesday that negotiations on tariffs will be held with Trump’s White House, not Congress. Canada’s focus, including in the budget, will be on “diversifying our trading relationships,” LeBlanc said. Both Trump and Carney have in recent days sounded optimistic about the prospects of a trade deal, but there were similarly rosy predictions in August before talks broke down. – Major projects – The budget is expected to allocate funds towards the major national projects Carney has tagged as crucial to Canadian economic sovereignty, including infrastructure for energy production and critical mineral mining. Champagne said there will also be support for workers hurt by Trump’s tariffs in sectors like autos and steel. The opposition is likely to raise alarm about deficit spending, but the deficit is expected to be lower than the CAN$78.3 billion ($56.3 billion) projected in Carney’s first budget last year. University of Ottawa political scientist Genevieve Tellier noted that implementation of the budget will in part depend on “the impact of tariffs,” particularly whether Trump’s levies cause further job losses. item.title: FG lists 5 digital banks Nigerians can use to access N50,000 monthly cash support
item.description: The Federal Government has listed five digital banks and mobile money platforms through which selected Nigerians can receive its N50,000 cash support under the National Emergency Relief and Stabilisation Intervention (NERSI). According to information published on the NERSI website, beneficiaries can access their funds through ALAT by Wema Bank, MoMo PSB, NairaGram, OPay and Moniepoint. The platforms provide USSD codes and mobile application options for beneficiaries to access their wallets and withdraw or spend the money. The government said beneficiaries would receive an SMS from their designated payment provider with instructions once their wallets had been credited. The five platforms and their access codes are: ALAT (Wema Bank): Dial 945 23#. MoMo (MoMo PSB): Dial 671 0#. NairaGram (Mobile wallet): Dial 726 00#. OPay (Mobile money): Dial 955 20# or use the OPay application. Moniepoint (Microfinance bank): Dial 5573 27# or use the Moniepoint application. How to receive the N50,000 support The NERSI website explained that the cash transfer is designed for poor and vulnerable Nigerian households, with beneficiaries selected through verified national identity records and the National Social Register. According to the programme’s guidelines, selected beneficiaries will receive an SMS from one of the five approved payment providers informing them of their selection. Recipients are required to reply YES to the message to give their consent to participate in the programme. Following confirmation, a mobile wallet linked to the beneficiary’s phone number and National Identification Number (NIN) will be opened, after which the N50,000 support will be credited. Beneficiaries can withdraw the money through a point-of-sale (POS) agent or at a bank, or spend directly from their mobile wallets. FG warns Nigerians against fraud The Federal Government stressed that participation in the programme is free and that beneficiaries are not required to pay any fee, register separately or visit government offices to secure the support. The NERSI website warned Nigerians against fraudsters demanding money to facilitate selection or release of the funds. It also advised beneficiaries not to disclose their personal identification numbers (PINs), one-time passwords (OTPs) or passwords to anyone, including agents and government officials. According to the programme’s guidelines, genuine messages will only come from ALAT, MoMo, NairaGram, OPay or Moniepoint and will only require beneficiaries to reply YES or dial their payment provider’s designated USSD code. The government further stated that not all eligible households would be included in the first batch of beneficiaries, adding that nobody could pay to secure a place on the list.
